title: BTL Y-wing (Star Wars, A New Hope / Rogue One)
intro: The Y-wing is a fictional fighter-bomber from the Star Wars films: a rugged Rebel craft with two long engine pods, laser cannons, an ion cannon turret and proton torpedoes. One pilot sits in a cockpit module at the front, with an astromech droid behind. Inside, the film's Y-wing looks much like the X-wing.

areas.name: Targeting scope
areas.text: The fold-down targeting display in front of the pilot's eyes.

panels.name: Targeting scope
panels.text: A small targeting display that swings down in front of the pilot's eyes, like the X-wing's.
panels.context: It is used for the precise attack on a small target.

controls.name: Targeting scope
controls.text: This display swings down to the pilot's eyes to help aim at a small target.
controls.context: In A New Hope the Gold squadron leader uses it during the trench run.

controls.name: Range readout
controls.text: Numbers on the scope show the distance to the target.
controls.context: The pilot fires when the distance is right.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: Screens and readouts in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: Screens and small lights in front of the pilot.
panels.context: They show the fighters around and the state of the ship.

controls.name: Sensor screen
controls.text: This screen shows nearby fighters and the target.
controls.context: It warns the pilot about enemy fighters that come close.

controls.name: Status lights
controls.text: Small lights show the state of the systems and any damage.
controls.context: The film does not explain each light; they tell the pilot whether the ship is healthy.

panels.name: Side consoles
panels.text: Switch panels on both sides of the seat and the turret control.
panels.context: The film shows the panels without naming each switch; the turret is described in the Databank.

controls.name: Switch banks
controls.text: Rows of toggle switches on both sides of the seat for the ship's systems.
controls.context: The film does not show what each switch does.

controls.name: Ion cannon turret control
controls.text: The Y-wing has an ion cannon turret behind the cockpit, a gun that disables ships instead of destroying them. In two-seat versions a gunner works it.
controls.context: The Databank describes the turret; how the pilot of a single-seat Y-wing controls it is not shown.

areas.name: Astromech socket
areas.text: The droid socket behind the cockpit.

panels.name: Astromech socket
panels.text: A socket behind the cockpit where an astromech droid rides along.
panels.context: The droid helps with navigation and repairs.

controls.name: Astromech droid
controls.text: A small robot in the socket helps with navigation and repairs during the flight.
controls.context: Like on the X-wing, the droid is a helper for the single pilot.

areas.name: Control yoke and throttle
areas.text: The hand controls the pilot flies with.

panels.name: Control yoke
panels.text: The two-handed control column the pilot steers with.
panels.context: The fire buttons sit on its grips.

controls.name: Control yoke
controls.text: Pushing the column forward or pulling it back tips the nose down or up; turning it rolls and banks the ship.
controls.context: It stands in front of the pilot and is held with both hands.

controls.name: Fire buttons
controls.text: Buttons on the control grips fire the laser cannons.
controls.context: The cannons sit at the front of the cockpit module.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: This stands for the control that sets the craft's speed.
panels.context: The film does not show this control clearly; the catalog adds it so a joystick set has a place for the speed.

controls.name: Throttle (not clearly shown)
controls.text: This axis stands for the craft's speed: forward for faster, back for slower. The screen does not show where the real control sits, so its place is a guess.
controls.context: On a stick and throttle set this is the throttle lever; in the work itself the pilot is mostly seen with both hands on the flight controls.
